Physical design

Tiqora-Serial has a clean layout at 1x2, the size info.yaml submits. The Tiny Tapeout gds, pre-flight and gate-level workflows pass on GitHub, and that run's own report gives the numbers in the table on this page (run 40624495043, src/ as on main 168fc84). It meets setup and hold timing at 50 MHz at all nine corners. No chip exists yet.

Three different areas

Die area

36,347 µm²: the 1x2 tile, 161.0 × 225.76 µm, from Tiny Tapeout's template tt_block_1x2_pg.def. Fixed by the tile count.

Core area

Where cells may go, inside the power ring: µm² measured, from LibreLane.

Summed cell area

21,322 µm² measured flat synthesis (make area, Yosys 0.33, the cells src/synth_exclude.cells leaves): 59% of the die. measured after placement, with timing-repair buffers, taps and clock tree but no fill: µm², of the core.

Where the cells go

Each block's cells, synthesized one module at a time and drawn to scale inside the 1x2 die outline. Positions mean nothing: this is proportion, not a floorplan.

The 1x2 layout

1x2 layout results

Explore the routed layout

Every cell where the placer put it and every wire the router drew: 3,109 cells that do the work, 2,092 more that only fill the rows (taps, fill and decoupling), and 21,094 wire segments, 72.6 mm of metal, on the 161.00 × 225.76 µm die. Each metal layer gets its own colour, and where layers cross, the colours add.

Scroll or pinch to zoom, drag to pan. With the keyboard: + and − zoom, arrows pan, 0 fits the die.

The clock button lights the clock tree the way an edge travels: from the clk pin through 4 levels of clock buffers (51 nets) to the 458 flip-flops, which flash when it arrives. Clock-tree buffers are drawn amber.

From a local LibreLane 3.0.14 run on sky130A (open_pdks 1.0.471), placement density 70%, read from the DEF after detailed routing and fill by docs/tools/routed_map.py. Wire segments per layer: met1 12,359 met2 7,830 met3 758 met4 147. It is not the GitHub run in the table above, whose layout cannot be downloaded from here: the placement differs in detail, and that local run, built with a different OpenROAD, missed setup at the slowest corner by 1.30 ns where GitHub's meets it by 1.43 ns.

Power: the run reports a power figure, but no switching activity from a real workload was given to it, so it is not shown. There is no power map.

Tiqora-Serial is Tiqora's timing unit with a serial host port instead of a processor, for a Tiny Tapeout 1x2 tile on SkyWater sky130. Nothing on these pages has run on real silicon or a real FPGA board; every number says how it was obtained.

Built by docs/tools/build_site.py from the RTL's own recordings and measurements. Maintained by @Normansrule. Source, tests and issues: github.com/Normansrule/tinytapeout-tiqora. Its sibling: Tiqora, the full microcontroller.
